# Zoning Analysis: 1500 W Wilson Ave, Chicago, IL
**PIN:** 14171060250000 | **Community Area:** Uptown (Area 3) | **Ward:** 47 (Ald. Matthew Martin, (773) 868-4747)

---

## 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B1-2** — a Neighborhood Shopping District at bulk/density level 2. This comes directly from the City's GIS zoning layer; you can verify it on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

> **Confidence:** High — this is a live GIS record. That said, zoning can be amended by ordinance, so confirm no pending map amendment with the Department of Planning and Development (DPD).

---

## 2. Apartments Above or On the Ground Floor?

**Above ground floor:** B1 districts are **Neighborhood Shopping Districts**, which — like B2 — are business districts that generally allow residential above the ground floor in Chicago's zoning framework. However, my retrieved code chunks speak directly to B2 [1] and B3 [1] regarding residential permissions. The B1 district's residential permissions are governed by § 17-3-0103-A (not retrieved in full), but B1 and B2 are closely related neighborhood commercial districts and B1 typically allows residential on upper floors.

**Ground-floor residential:** B1 districts are oriented toward ground-floor retail/commercial uses. Under the general B/C district framework [1], [4], ground-floor residential is generally not a primary permitted use — it is the commercial ground floor that defines B1. Ground-floor conversion of commercial to residential in a multi-story building requires Zoning Administrator approval [3] under § 17-13-1003-NN. A standalone detached house or two-flat at ground level is further restricted near transit [4] (see Section 5 below).

> **Confidence:** Moderate. The retrieved chunks confirm B2/B3 residential rules [1] and ground-floor conversion procedures [3], but the **specific B1-2 use table** (§ 17-3-0200 and the B1 use allowances) was **not retrieved**. You should confirm the exact residential use permissions directly in § 17-3-0103-A and the B1 use table via [Chicago Municipal Code online](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/chicago_il/0-0-0-563405) or by contacting DPD's Zoning Help Desk at (312) 744-5777.

---

## 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards

The **"-2" suffix** is the bulk/density designator. Per [3] (§ 17-3-0403), all B and C district development is subject to maximum FAR standards that vary by district letter and dash number. The specific FAR table for B1-2 is referenced in § 17-3-0403-A but the **numeric table itself was not included** in the retrieved chunks. Similarly, minimum lot area per dwelling unit, maximum building height, and setback standards are set out in § 17-3-0400 series and § 17-3-0500 series, which were **not fully retrieved**.

What the code does confirm:
- FAR standards for B and C districts are set in **§ 17-3-0403-A** [3], with the dash number (here, -2) controlling the applicable maximum.
- FAR increases for transit-served locations in **B-3 and C-3** districts are possible under § 17-3-0403-B [3], but this parcel is **B1-2, not B-3** — so that specific FAR boost mechanism does not directly apply in its current form.
- Residential density (minimum lot area per unit) is governed by § 17-3-0404 (not retrieved).

> **How to verify:** Pull the full B1-2 bulk standards from [Chicago Municipal Code § 17-3-0400 Table](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/chicago_il/0-0-0-563405) or request a **Zoning Certificate of Use** from DPD. The zoning map linked above also links to district summaries.

> **Confidence:** Low on specific numbers — I cannot state the FAR, height limit, or MLA figures because the numeric tables were not in the retrieved context, and I will not fabricate them.

---

## 4. Overlays and Special Designations

This parcel carries **four regulatory overlays**, all confirmed from the city's GIS overlay layers:

- **Transit-Oriented Development — CTA Rail.** The parcel is within a CTA TOD area (the Montrose Brown Line station is just 0.44 miles away; the Ravenswood Metra station is 0.4 miles away). This triggers the Connected Communities Ordinance TOD provisions, enabling potential density and parking bonuses. New construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA or Metra rail station entrance must satisfy the specific criteria of [4] (§ 17-3-0308), including compliance with transit-served location standards under § 17-10-0102-B and pedestrian street standards under § 17-3-0504.

- **Transit-Oriented Development — Metra.** The parcel is also within a Metra TOD overlay, reflecting the nearby Ravenswood Metra station.

- **ADU Eligible Area.** Accessory Dwelling Units are permitted here under Chicago's ADU ordinance (§ 17-2-0303 and related sections). This allows coach houses and conversion ADUs on eligible properties.

- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone.** Any residential development or conversion triggering the ARO (generally 10+ units or an "entitlement") requires affordable unit set-asides [2] (§ 2-44-085). The Uptown community area already has 20 ARO-related affordable housing projects totaling 976 units, including large developments like Ruth Shriman House (231 units), Leland Apts. (137 units), and Harold Washington Apts. (100 units). For transit-served locations providing ≥50% of required affordable units on-site, supplemental incentives (additional FAR and height) are available in B-3 and C-3 districts [2] — though again, this parcel is B1-2, so a rezoning would be needed to access the full B-3/C-3 supplemental bonus stack.

**No** Planned Development, landmark/historic district (local or national register), lakefront protection overlay, Special Service Area, or Special District designation applies to this parcel.

**Flood Zone:** FEMA Zone X — Area of Minimal Flood Hazard. This parcel is **not** in a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not federally required. No brownfield sites are nearby.

> **Confidence:** High on overlay presence/absence — these are official GIS determinations. Verify effective ordinance numbers with DPD, as overlay boundaries can be updated.

---

## 5. Parking Requirements and Transit Reductions

The parcel's TOD-CTA and TOD-Metra overlays, combined with its proximity to the Montrose Brown Line (0.44 mi) and Ravenswood Metra (0.4 mi), make it eligible for **parking reductions under the Connected Communities Ordinance**. Under [4] (§ 17-3-0308) and the TOD standards at § 17-10-0102-B, projects in transit-served locations within 2,640 feet of a CTA or Metra rail station entrance may qualify for reduced — or in some cases eliminated — minimum parking requirements.

The **specific parking minimums** for B1-2 (set out in § 17-3-0500 and Table 17-3-0504) and the **exact TOD parking reduction percentage** were **not in the retrieved code chunks**.

> **How to verify:** See § 17-10-0102-B and the parking tables in § 17-3-0500. DPD's Connected Communities summary is also available at [chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/connected-communities-ordinance](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/connected-communities-ordinance.html).
